newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Refining aims to save 25 pct in labour costs.
newsitem.headline: NZ Refining aims to save 25 pct in labour costs.

text.p: The New Zealand Refining Co Ltd is carrying out a review of its organisation with the objective of saving 25 percent of overall labour-related costs, chairman Jim Law said on Thursday.
"The team carrying out this review are working towards recommending a more efficient organisational structure by the end of June for implementation by year end," Law told the annual meeting.
A comprehensive review of the total operations of the refinery had also been completed and a number of areas of potential savings identified which the company would investigate over the coming year.
It was further anticipated that some savings would be made in energy conservation and efficiency.
"These initiatives will enable us to maintain our position in the top quartile of efficient refineries in South East Asia," Law said.
Although margins had been "very weak" in January and February, they had improved through March and the oil refiner was well placed for the balance of 1997.

Law said the company carried out a successful 'C' Block shutdown in February for statutory inspection, maintenance and new catalyst loading, but all plant was expected to be available and in good order for the rest of the year.
"We are well placed, therefore, to exploit whatever opportunities the market may present."
Law said the strong New Zealand dollar had diluted margins in the latter part of 1996, but the company believed this was an external factor it had to live with.

"A major factor influencing the value of our processing income is the exchange rate with the U.S. dollar given that the key components of crude and product prices are denominated in U.S. dollars," Law said.
"The benefit of the strong U.S. dollar margins in the latter part of 1996 was diluted when converted to New Zealand dollars.
"We believe this is an external factor we have to live with and continue to develop our business plans to ensure that we can remain highly competitive even if the currency markets move against us."

NZ Refining is owned by local units of Mobil Corp (19.20 percent), The British Petroleum Co Plc (23.66 percent) and Royal Dutch Petroleum Co (17.14 percent). Fletcher Challenge Petroleum, a unit of Fletcher Energy has 14.20 percent and a further 11.35 percent is held by Caltex Petroleum Corp, a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
